html:
The Yemeni civil war began in September 2014, when the Houthi movement, a Zaydi rebel group from the north, took the capital Sana'a. In March 2015 a coalition led by Saudi Arabia began bombing to restore the ousted government.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, held the north and most of the people. The coalition, with the UAE, held the south and east through local allies, including southern separatists. Air strikes, blockade and fighting wrecked the economy. Famine threatened and cholera spread, making it one of the worst humanitarian crises of the century.

A truce in 2022 cut the fighting but did not end the war. From late 2023 the Houthis attacked shipping in the Red Sea over the war in Gaza. See also the Zaydi imamate.
